nodes.name: NF surface oxide removal
nodes.procedure: NF (1 × 1 cm², 1.5 mm thick, GJY-NI001, GJY) was sonicated in an aqueous hydrochloric acid solution which consisted of 1:1 vol ratio of deionized water (18.2 MΩ cm, ULUPURE) and concentrated hydrochloric acid (HCl, 36-38%, SCR) to remove surface oxides. The NF was then rinsed successively with deionized water and ethanol (C₂H₅OH, 97%, SCR), and finally dried in oven at 60 °C. Unless specified, all the samples were prepared on the as-treated NF substrates.

nodes.name: Ni nanocluster electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Ni nanoclusters were deposited onto [pretreated] NF substrate via a simple electrochemical method. A three-electrode system was employed for the electrodeposition, which comprised of a piece of NF as working electrode, a graphite rod as counter electrode and a Hg/Hg₂SO₄ (saturated K₂SO₄, CHI 151, CH Instruments) as reference electrode. The plating solution contained aqueous 0.5 M Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O (98%, SCR) and 0.5 M H₃BO₃ (99.5%, SCR). The Ni nanoclusters were electrodeposited onto the NF substrate at a constant potential at -2 V vs. Hg/Hg₂SO₄ for 600 s. Kindly note that the HER performance of Ni/NF was measured immediately after its synthesis to avoid oxidation of the sample surface.

nodes.name: CV activation of Ni/NF
nodes.procedure: Cyclic-voltammetric treatment was performed on the freshly prepared Ni/NF sample in aqueous 1 M KOH (99.99%, Aladdin) electrolyte in a three-electrode setup. A graphite rod and a Hg/HgO electrode (1 M KOH, CHI 152, CH Instruments) were used as counter and reference electrodes, respectively. A freshly prepared Ni/NF was treated by repeated CV in the potential range of −0.675 to 0.125 V vs. RHE (RHE: reversible hydrogen electrode; unless specifically stated, all potentials in this work are cited with respect to RHE) at a scan rate of 100 mV/s for 25 cycles to obtain the CeNi/NF sample. The HER performance of CeNi/NF was measured immediately after its synthesis.

nodes.characterization_summary: A-Ni/NF surface shows nanoclusters aggregated by ~10-30 nm sized particles (Fig. 2a(i)). AC-Ni/NF exhibits both nanowires and nanoclusters (Fig. 2b(i)).
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM analyses revealed that A-Ni/NF surface was composed of nanoclusters aggregated by ~10e30 nm sized particles (Fig. 2a(i)). The SEM image of AC-Ni/NF showed a different morphology from the A-Ni/NF sample, which exhibited both nanowires and nanoclusters (Fig. 2b(i)).

nodes.characterization_summary: A-Ni/NF consists of Ni(0) grains (Fig. 2a(iii)). AC-Ni/NF composed of connected Ni(0) and Ni(OH)2 rods/flakes with abundant Ni(0)·Ni(OH)2 interfaces (Fig. 2b(ii-iii)).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) analysis indicated that the A-Ni/NF sample was consisted of Ni (0) grains (Fig. 2a(iii))... AC-Ni/NF surface was composed of connected Ni (0) and Ni (OH) 2 rods/flakes, hence with abundant Ni (0)⋅Ni (OH) 2 interfaces (Fig. 2b(ii-iii)).

nodes.characterization_summary: A-Ni/CC shows only Ni(0) patterns (PDF#65-0380). AC-Ni/CC exhibits Ni(0) signals plus obvious Ni(OH)2 reflections (PDF#14-0117).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrodeposited Ni particles on carbon cloth (A-Ni/CC) only showed XRD patterns of Ni (0) (PDF#65e0380), while the AC-Ni/CC exhibited obvious reflections from Ni (OH) 2 species (PDF#14e0117) in addition to the Ni^(0) signals (Fig. 3).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms increased Ni(OH)2 ratio in AC-Ni/NF compared to A-Ni/NF. Ni(OH)2 signals detected on A-Ni/NF surface layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS characterizations also confirmed an increased ratio of Ni (OH) 2 in the AC-Ni/NF sample (Supporting Information Fig. S3, Table S2). Note that signals from Ni (OH) 2 species were also recorded on the A-Ni/NF sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman during ageing of AC-Ni/NF shows broad β-Ni(OH)2 band 400-560 cm⁻¹ appearing at 10 min, peaking at 30 min (Fig. 4).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As the ageing time increased to No. 10 min, a broad band between 400−560 cm⁻¹ was recorded. This band further increased and reached a maximum in the intensity as the ageing time went up to 30 min.

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-Ni/NF Rct = 0.6 Ω, close to Pt/C/NF and much lower than other Ni samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Rct of the AC-Ni/NF (0.6) was very close to that of the benchmark Pt/C/NF while significantly lower than those of the Ni/NF, CeNi/NF, and A-Ni/NF catalysts.

nodes.characterization_summary: During HER on AC-Ni/NF, β-Ni(OH)2 bands at 448 cm⁻¹ (A1g) and 517 cm⁻¹ (2nd acoustic) attenuate but persist to -0.075 V, regenerate after potential removal (Fig. 6).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the peaks at 448 and 517 cm⁻¹ were assigned to A1g and 2nd acoustic vibrational modes of β-Ni (OH) 2... These two bands further decreased in intensity as the potential was swept to the HER range of ~0 V ∼ -0.075 V... can still be observed even at a H2-evolving potential of -0.075 V.
